correctness.rationale: The ordinary knight graph has 16 vertices and 24 undirected edges; exact independent-set enumeration yields 1364 nonempty simplices with f-vector (16,96,276,412,340,170,48,6). A deterministically specified sequence of 16 pivot matchings produces 679 disjoint Hasse-cover pairs, and ALL 5772 cover arrows on the 1364-face poset admit a topological ordering, so the discrete-Morse matching is acyclic, with precisely one critical vertex and five critical three-faces. The integral CW reduction has no possible nonzero attaching maps and is a wedge of five three-spheres. For sizes at most three the graph has an isolated vertex or no attack edges, hence the independence complex is a cone or simplex. For each of eight geometric square symmetries, independent signed fixed-simplex enumeration gives Lefschetz numbers (-4,2,0,2,-2,2,-2,2), hence character (5,-1,1,-1,3,-1,3,-1); the stated 1+2+2 representation matches all traces. Program replay from its included path succeeds. Mod-2 ranks are a cross-check and are never treated as integral proof.

originality.rationale: This identifies a different invariant than classic enumerations or chess-graph gonality: the smallest noncontractible square knight-placement independence complex, its exact integral homotopy type, and all eight natural dihedral homology traces. The closest same-object arXiv full text calculates knight graph gonality and does not give homotopy or symmetry homology. The closest general topological full text uses nearest-neighbor grid graphs, not knight adjacency. The published periodic four-by-four knight graph is a four-cube with 32 edges, whereas the nonperiodic ordinary graph has 24; its known seven-sphere calculation neither identifies nor implies our five-sphere theorem or character. Independent-set tables give the face-total 1365 but not differential topology or equivariance. Actual semantic record searches by aliases, statements, parameters and stronger coverage showed no exact/stronger result. This is evidence of noncoverage in the inspected material, not a proof of bibliographic uniqueness.
residual_risks: Equivalent unindexed or older work might not have been retrieved; negative search is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: A canonical chess-graph family has a genuine topological cutoff: its first noncontractible square-board instance is size four, with a complete integer homotopy classification, rather than merely a count of knight placements. The six critical-cell certificate explains why the high-dimensional nonpure face system collapses to five 3-spheres; the dihedral character and 1-dimensional invariant subspace reveal symmetry information not recoverable from homology rank or independence polynomial. Its distinction between open and periodic boundary conditions gives a natural benchmark for later computations in this family. The exact case is mathematically motivated; no unwarranted extension to larger boards is claimed.
